Subject: Offline Deployment Simulation + Rollback Drill - EdgeSafe pilot

Amit —

Following up from last week's call: we'd like to run a full offline deployment simulation (air-gapped) for the EdgeSafe pilot at your test site on Sep 9. The simulation scope is: deliver signed offline artifacts, perform operator-side verification, do the install, then execute a controlled rollback to validate the recovery path.

Objectives
- Validate image signing verification and manifest ingestion on-site
- Measure end-to-end install time and KV-cache warmup behavior
- Execute rollback path and confirm operator checkpoints (activation token revoke, image reversion)

Proposed timeline (all local time)
- 09:00 — arrival, operator brief and handshake
- 09:30 — preflight checks + manifest verification
- 10:15 — artifact install (no external network)
- 12:00 — lunch and telemetry review (local logs only)
- 13:00 — rollback drill and final signoff

I've attached the offline-sim-checklist.pdf and a draft recovery-playbook-v1.2.docx for your ops team. Can you confirm the onsite operator list (names + PGP key fingerprints or KMS key IDs) and whether the safety officer will be available for the rollback window? Also confirm if you want the manifest signed by Redwood KMS or with a customer-supplied signing key — both options are supported.

If this schedule works we'll lock the window and ship the pre-signed bundle via our courier and register the manifest in the sealed transfer ledger (offline receipt required).

Thanks,

Amit / Sofia —

Short answers to Amit's questions and a technical plan attached. See signed-image-manifest.json (stub) and the verification checklist in the attachment. Key points:

1) Activation tokens — we will use an asymmetric per-operator flow. Redwood will sign a time-limited activation envelope with our KMS; the envelope includes the operator public key fingerprint. Operators can then use their private key to unwrap. No symmetric keys are transmitted.

2) Dual-signer manifest — supported. The manifest will contain: image SHA256 (uncompressed), Redwood attestation (our KMS signature block), and a second signature field for EdgeSafe KMS. For the drill we'll include a placeholder EdgeSafe signature (you can replace with your KMS signature during handoff).

3) Offline checksum validation — we'll include a detached .sha256 file and a small verification binary (linux x64) that validates signatures using bundled public keys. The verification binary runs fully offline and exits with codes documented in the checklist.

Operational notes:
- Manifest filename: signed-image-manifest.json (attached)
- Verification steps: (i) verify detached checksum against image; (ii) verify Redwood signature; (iii) verify customer signature (if present); (iv) run container unpack smoke tests
- Rollback approach: mark the current image as revoked in the local manifest and re-activate previous image ID using operator private key + revocation nonce. We include a recovery-playbook-v1.2.docx with the step-by-step commands.

I've also linked SUP-4123 for telemetry capture and evidence collection items. Recommend a 30-minute security walkthrough before the install window where we demo the verification binary and show logs that will be captured locally.

Jonas

Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
